_doc: CODEC FIELD SURVIVAL -- the shared matrix that says, per codec and per field,
whether an attribute-SATURATED element survives a round trip.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Every codec gate in this repository (SVG parse, SVG
round-trip, canonical test-JSON round-trip, binary round-trip) compares
`document_to_test_json` STRINGS before and after. That catches a dropped field
perfectly -- but only for fields the canonical test-JSON itself emits. Measured
on this commit by round-tripping one saturated Path through all three codecs in
both ports: the set of fields the BINARY codec drops is a strict SUBSET of the
set the canonical test-JSON drops. So no fixture, however saturated, can
red-light a single one of the binary codec's drops through the existing gates.
The corpus census's prescription (§5.4: 'one maximal fixture per element
type') is therefore NOT EXECUTABLE against the string oracle -- a saturated
fixture would be normalized back to default on the way in and pass, green and
vacuous.
This family sidesteps the string oracle. Both ports build the same saturated
Path IN CODE (the shape is spelled out in `saturated_path` below, and mirrored
in jas_dioxus/src/cross_language_test.rs and JasSwift/Tests/CrossLanguageTests
.swift), round-trip it, and compare field values at the MODEL level (Rust
PartialEq / Swift Equatable). The matrix below is then asserted cell by cell.
HOW TO READ A CELL. PRESERVED = the field came back equal. DROPPED = it did
not. A DROPPED cell is a PINNED gap, not an accepted one: fixing the site turns
this gate RED until the cell is updated, so a gap here can never rot into a
silent suppression (the same discipline as `expected_violations` in
test_fixtures/preservation/).
THE PRESERVATION LAW (transcripts/EDIT_SEMANTICS_FREEZE.md, ratified
2026-07-27) frames every DROPPED cell: a round trip speaks to NOTHING, so it
must preserve EVERYTHING. `classification` therefore separates the two shapes
the law distinguishes, and the distinction is evidence-based, not editorial:
REPRESENTABLE_BUT_DROPPED -- the output representation demonstrably carries
this class of value ALREADY, somewhere this codebase can be pointed at (an
attribute one port writes, an attribute this port's own reader parses, or a
slot the format has been extended with before). Dropping it is a defect.
NO_COUNTERPART -- the output representation has no construct for the value
and neither port writes an extension for it. An honest representation
limit, which the law says must be DOCUMENTED rather than guessed at.
`classification` is prose analysis and is NOT machine-asserted; only
`survival` and `port_overrides` are.

saturated_path._doc: The element both ports construct in code. Recorded here so the two mirrors can be diffed against one statement of intent; it is NOT parsed by either gate (the canonical test-JSON cannot express most of these keys -- that is the whole point).
saturated_path.fill_gradient: radial, angle 45, aspect 200, smooth, dither, along-stroke, 2 stops
saturated_path.stroke_gradient: radial, angle 45, aspect 200, smooth, dither, along-stroke, 2 stops

port_overrides._doc: A cell where the two ports MEASURABLY DISAGREE today. The `survival` value above is what both ports must reach; a port listed here is asserted to produce the stated OTHER value, so closing the divergence turns this gate red until the entry is deleted. Empty is the goal state.

test_json._all_dropped: REPRESENTABLE_BUT_DROPPED. The canonical test-JSON is a hand-built object writer that already emits nested objects (`transform`, `fill`, `stroke`, `tspans`) and already emits keys CONDITIONALLY on non-default (`id`, and `fill_rule` -- the one PRESERVED row here, written only when `evenodd`). Nothing about the format prevents any of these keys; the writer simply has none. THIS IS THE BLINDNESS MECHANISM: every codec gate compares test-JSON strings, so each DROPPED row here makes the corresponding row in `binary` and `svg` unreachable by any fixture. The binary codec's dropped set is a strict SUBSET of this one.
test_json.fill_rule: PRESERVED -- written at jas_dioxus/src/geometry/test_json.rs `o.str_val("fill_rule", "evenodd")` and mirrored in JasSwift/Sources/Geometry/TestJson.swift. It is the proof that the conditional-key mechanism works and generalises.

binary._all_dropped: REPRESENTABLE_BUT_DROPPED. The binary codec is msgpack over per-tag positional arrays; it has been EXTENDED TWICE by appending slots (the `symbols` master store at document index 3, tolerated via `arr.get(3)`; the live-element instance transform at TAG_LIVE slot 9). The mechanism is established and in use, so these seven fields are omitted, not unrepresentable. `pack_common` carries 6 of CommonProps' 9 fields (jas_dioxus/src/geometry/binary.rs, JasSwift/Sources/Geometry/Binary.swift); `mode`, `mask` and `tool_origin` are hard-coded to defaults on the unpack side. Live consequence: apply a brush or set a blend mode, relaunch, and the setting is gone.
binary.stroke.dash_align_anchors: PRESERVED -- pack_stroke carries the full Stroke including dash pattern, dash length, align, miter limit and both arrowheads. The census row that grouped `dash_align_anchors` and `width_points` with the binary codec's losses is corrected here by measurement: they survive.
binary._stroke_all: stroke.align, stroke.dash_pattern and stroke.miter_limit are PRESERVED for the same reason: pack_stroke is complete. The binary codec is the ONLY one of the three that carries the whole Stroke.
binary.width_points: PRESERVED -- packed for Line and Path.

svg.common.tool_origin: REPRESENTABLE_BUT_DROPPED (Rust, until this wave). `jas:tool-origin` is written by JasSwift's <path> arm AND parsed by Rust's own `parse_common` for every element -- so the representation exists, this port's reader consumes it, and only this port's writer omitted it. Closed in the same wave as this fixture.
svg.common.mask: NO_COUNTERPART as things stand. SVG has <mask>, but neither port writes or reads any mask construct, and jas's Mask carries `invert`, `disabled`, `linked` and `unlink_transform` with no SVG analogue. Documented, not guessed.
svg.common.mode: NO_COUNTERPART as things stand. CSS `mix-blend-mode` covers the 16 modes, but neither port writes or reads it.
svg.fill_gradient: NO_EXACT_COUNTERPART. SVG <linearGradient>/<radialGradient> exist, but jas's Gradient carries `midpoint_to_next` per stop plus `aspect_ratio`, `dither` and `stroke_sub_mode`, none of which SVG expresses. A faithful export needs a jas: extension alongside the standard element -- a design question, not a one-line fix.
svg.stroke_gradient: NO_EXACT_COUNTERPART -- as fill_gradient, plus the stroke sub-mode has no SVG meaning at all.
svg.stroke_brush: NO_COUNTERPART as things stand. A jas-private reference ("<library>/<brush>"); it would ride a jas: attribute exactly as tool-origin does, but no port writes one.
svg.stroke_brush_overrides: NO_COUNTERPART as things stand -- same shape as stroke_brush.
svg.width_points: NO_COUNTERPART as things stand. The variable-width profile has no SVG stroke analogue; a faithful export means emitting the OUTLINE, which is a different document, or a jas: extension.
svg.fill_rule: PRESERVED -- both ports write `fill-rule="evenodd"` and both read it.
svg.stroke.dash_align_anchors: PRESERVED -- both ports write `data-jas-dash-align-anchors="true"` and both read it.
svg.stroke.dash_pattern: PRESERVED as of CODECSAT. It was REPRESENTABLE_BUT_DROPPED in BOTH ports: `stroke-dasharray` is a STANDARD SVG presentation attribute and neither port wrote it or read it, so a dashed stroke saved to SVG came back SOLID while the jas-private flag saying HOW to lay the dashes out was carried faithfully. NOTE ON THE FIXTURE'S OWN VALUES: SVG lengths are written in px at 4 decimal places, so a pt value whose px form is not exact at 4dp does not come back bit-equal (4pt -> 5.3333px -> 3.999975pt). The saturated pattern is 3 / 1.5 / 6 / 0.75 pt = 4 / 2 / 8 / 1 px exactly, so this cell reads DROPPED only for an OMISSION and never for a rounding. Every other SVG length in this document has the same ~1e-5 property; the string-oracle gates absorb it because canonical test-JSON rounds to 4dp.
svg.stroke.miter_limit: PRESERVED as of CODECSAT. It was REPRESENTABLE_BUT_DROPPED in BOTH ports: `stroke-miterlimit` is a STANDARD SVG presentation attribute; neither port wrote it and each reader hard-coded 10.0. Unitless, so no px conversion and no rounding question.
svg.stroke.align: NO_COUNTERPART as things stand. Inside/outside stroke alignment has no attribute in SVG 1.1 (`stroke-alignment` is an unshipped SVG 2 draft), so a faithful export needs a jas: extension -- which is a naming decision, not a repair, and is banked rather than guessed.
